# ACC011 `acc-collapse-imperfect-nest`

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

`collapse(n)` on OpenACC loops that are not tightly nested.

## Why

`collapse(n)` merges the iteration spaces of n nested loops into one. The specification requires the
loops to be tightly nested: no statement between the loop headers or between the `end do`s. Compilers
reject some violations and mishandle others (the extra statements executed once per collapsed
iteration, or not at all). Move the statements inside the innermost loop, or collapse fewer levels.

## Reported

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop collapse(2)
do j = 1, m
  c = coef(j)          ! between the loop headers
  do i = 1, n
    a(i, j) = c * b(i, j)
  end do
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop collapse(2)

    do j = 1, m
      do i = 1, n
        a(i, j) = coef(j) * b(i, j)
      end do
    end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC011] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC011` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
